body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: DioxusDocument's two render sites, initial_build (vdom.rebuild) and poll (vdom.render_immediate), run the vdom into a buffer of 0.7 WriteMutations calls with the document unborrowed, then borrow the document once, replay the buffer through the existing MutationWriter and flush the queued mounted events as before.
So user code run during render (a component body, a polled task) can call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) with no RefCell already borrowed panic; an engine change for every DioxusDocument, the stand and the windowed dioxus-native launch included.
Ports upstream's test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document as the witness: a task spawned during a re-render calls set_focus(true) and get_client_rect() and the focused node is the input it named.
Inverts dioxus_runtime_probe's two should_panic pins into tests that a key-handler-spawned task's set_focus moves focus without panic, in both layout modes, the handle held and the key target focused by Tab still asserted first.
Re-asserts unchanged behaviour through the existing checks: the document each render builds, element ids, snapshot and diff, mounted events' order and incremental/non-incremental layout identity (stand_*, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle, dioxus_runtime_probe's other eight tests).

body_fields.what: the two render sites initial_build and poll, and the ported test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document in its mod tests

DioxusState, if the buffer lives on it as upstream's does; otherwise kept byte-identical to upstream at 434e0661

body: DioxusDocument's render path (initial_build and poll): the document is borrowed once after the vdom renders, so every mutation of a render reaches the engine through MutationWriter in recorded order.
Focus moved by MountedData set_focus from a task polled during render: the engine's focused node must become the named input, with no panic, in both layout modes.

The engine's changed set (changed_nodes): an in-document mutation and a focus change mark it; the replayed buffer and a render-time set_focus must still mark it so a poll that takes a non-empty set rebuilds the accessibility tree.

Accessibility tree refresh through the Document::accessibility_tree trait method, so DioxusDocument's override (its stable ids) still reaches the tree on InitialTreeRequested and on change, headless on the stand in both layout modes.
Stable element ids as AccessKit author_id on every element node of a Dioxus document: the buffer carries ids and must leave each element's id as the direct write gave it.
The snapshot model reading role, name, focus and states from accessibility_tree, and its diff: unchanged by the buffered render.
The actionable-key rule and DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable returning nothing on every stand task: author keys must survive the replay unchanged.

Falsy Dioxus values of the bridge's 28 boolean attributes (disabled, hidden, inert among them) removing the attribute on both attribute paths of MutationWriter: the replay must route set-attribute calls through the same paths.
HTML focus fixup on the mutator flush: a focused node coming under inert gives up focus as the mutator flushes; the replay must still flush so the fixup runs once per applied buffer.
The tree's focus falling back to the window where the focused node was not built: a set_focus issued during render, before the buffer is applied, must not leave the tree's focus on an unbuilt node.
Tab key focus as the inverted pins' precondition: the key target focused by Tab through the harness's press, read back before the spawned task's set_focus.
Mounted events (flush_queued_mounted_events) flushed after the buffer is applied, their order unchanged, so a MountedData handle is held only for nodes in the document.
Both layout modes (incremental and non-incremental) and their identity: the inverted pins run one per mode and the layout identity stays as it is.
The windowed dioxus-native launch renders through the same buffer; its accessibility tree refresh to the platform adapter is read, not run, as the probe's windowed path was.
The buffer holds ids, tag and attribute names and text in process only, never printed or logged: no new log field or span for blitz* or escher_* targets.

body_fields.convention: a focus check reads the engine's focus, the snapshot's focused node and the tree's focus and asserts they agree at each step
a headless stand or bridge check of focus or the tree runs in both layout modes
a check reading has_changes() as "this step changed something" drains the changed set first, a fresh harness document's set being non-empty

Role derivation and ARIA state attributes (aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-checked, aria-invalid, aria-expanded, aria-disabled, aria-level): the builder is not touched.
Accessible names and descriptions (aria-label, aria-labelledby, label binding, aria-describedby): the builder's name reads are not touched.
The select control's keys, list opening, typeahead and optgroup, and the range input's keys: no control's key or pointer handling changes.
Per-surface keyboard shortcuts of seven_guis CRUD and Cells, and the CRUD listbox's unread aria-activedescendant: no stand app changes.
Password and file input masking (MASKED_VALUE) and the driver's disabled refusal of click and type: no driver verb or snapshot field changes.
Platform adapter creation before the window is shown (accesskit_xplat) and the windowed AT witness of residual res-llkgqygv: no adapter is built or moved.
Hidden content and inert hit-testing rules (aria-hidden, hidden, display none, visibility hidden): no visibility rule changes.
Cognitive error recovery (the flight booker's invalid dates) and motion: no stand cue or animation changes.
Language and direction, text alternatives in fixtures and IME: no fixture or text input path changes.
Escher's visual lint (Session::lint) and its contrast reading: not touched.

body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the shell builds and refreshes the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree`, so DioxusDocument's override reaches it, and every Dioxus element node carries its stable element id as `author_id` (no TextRun / root / Window node does); this is the id contract the buffered replay must reproduce element for element, and the trait-method path the replayed render must still feed.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — `DioxusDocument::snapshot` takes role, name and the focused node from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns, with no second mapping; nothing focused at boot, only `back-btn` after one move; the snapshot's `focused` reading the inverted pins assert must keep coming from the tree, not from a mapping of the chunk's own.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — founded the actionable-key rule and `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` (gated by `accessibility`); trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or role, since that moves the pinned Tab order; the replay must carry every author key so the check stays empty.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — a falsy Dioxus boolean attribute is removed on both attribute paths (dynamic and static template), so `hidden: false` keeps a node in the tree; and the Tab / Shift+Tab key-press focus check (`crud-name` → `crud-surname`, `back-btn` on first Tab) with the focused node equal to the tree's focus; the replay must route set-attribute calls through both `MutationWriter` paths, and this check is the shape of the inverted pins' Tab precondition.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — made the tree refresh on change real: `View::poll` takes `changed_nodes` (outside the cfg) and rebuilds the tree on a non-empty set; `changed_nodes` marked by in-document mutation, focus or checked change, a text input, not node creation; before this the flag answered false and the tree was built once — the precedent for the trap that a buffered replay that skipped marking would silently freeze the tree.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the founder ratified the refresh on change and the changed-set contract (and the bridge's falsy boolean clear); these are ratified engine contracts the buffered render may not move without a new ruling.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a freshly booted document's set is non-empty from the boot's own mutations, so a check reading `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first; binds any new check on the buffered path's changed set (the extract's anti-pattern).

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — the stand's role and name expectations are stated once in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` (`controls`, `INPUT_NAMES`, `rendered`), never a second mapping; the ported test and inverted pins must assert through the existing tree and snapshot, not tables of their own.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom, so both stand binaries (`seven_guis_native`, `escher-session`) compile the override, snapshot, text and diff, neither a platform adapter; the new buffer module lands in a crate both binaries build under that feature, so it must stay ungated while the gated items keep reaching them.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the stand's states entry) — the flight booker's date inputs state `aria-invalid` and the invalid cue (Book's `disabled`) is read without colour; these reach the snapshot only through the replayed set-attribute paths, the falsy removal included.

**2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces** — autofocus focuses the latest mounted focusable node whose `autofocus` is present and not "false", applied on flush, and the bridge removes a falsy `autofocus`; the buffered render's single flush after the replay must keep that flush-time focus step.

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** — the falsy predicate became upstream's 28-name `is_bool_attr`, the bridge's own list retired, leaving `mutation_writer.rs` byte-identical to upstream at `434e0661` (the baseline the scope keeps); a falsy `inert` is removed; a change to `mutation_writer.rs` (e.g. hosting the buffer on `DioxusState`) breaks that identity and must be named with its reason.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** (both entries) — Enter / Space dispatch a Click whose Dioxus `onclick` runs then `handle_click`, `counter-increment`, `flight-book`, `crud-create` changing the screen (a re-render through `poll`, the site the chunk edits); `stand_keyboard` built with its triple focus agreement and `disabled` read by presence; the walks and activation rows are the witness the buffered render must leave green.

- a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (Accessibility tree lifecycle) requires the tree to be rebuilt from a poll that takes a non-empty changed set through `Document::accessibility_tree`, so DioxusDocument's stable-id override reaches it; the buffered replay into `MutationWriter` must leave the same `changed_nodes` marks as the direct write did. Whether a replay applied after `render_immediate` marks the same set is research's question.
- a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (Accessibility tree lifecycle) states that a focus change marks the changed set; a `set_focus` from a task polled during render, now reachable with no panic, must mark the node so the tree's focus refreshes at the next poll.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (Accessibility tree output) requires every element node in a Dioxus document to carry its stable element id as AccessKit `author_id`, and the tree the shell hands the adapter to equal the harness's tree node for node; the buffer must replay the same element ids in the same order.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (Accessibility tree output) requires `DioxusDocument::snapshot` to take role, name, focus and states from `accessibility_tree`, and the actionable-key rule requires `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` to return nothing on every stand task; neither may move under the buffered render.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Test harness pattern) requires the engine's focus, the snapshot's `focused` node and the tree's focus to agree at every step of `stand_keyboard`'s walks in both layout modes.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Focus order per layout) requires HTML's focus fixup (a focused node coming under `inert` gives focus up as the mutator flushes) to keep working; with the flush now done in one borrow after the buffer, whether the fixup still runs at the same point is research's question.

- `stand_keyboard`'s triple focus agreement (engine focus, snapshot `focused`, tree focus) per step in both layout modes, per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Test harness pattern) — the model for the inverted pins' focus assertion.
- The harness's focused-node query (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:107-115`), per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract (Focus management test harness).
- `inert_subtree`'s check that the tree's focus falls back to the window where the focused node was not built, per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract — the regression witness for the focus fixup under the new flush order.
- A check that reads `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first, per a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (Accessibility tree lifecycle) — applies to any new check on the buffered path's changed set.

- No second role or name mapping: the roles and names checks expect are stated once in the shared module's tables, per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (Accessibility tree output); the ported test and the inverted pins assert focus through the existing tree and snapshot, not a mapping of their own.
- Do not read a fresh harness document's non-empty changed set as proof that the buffered render marked a change; drain first, per a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy (Accessibility tree lifecycle).

- a11y ↔ tests: the `a11y` CI leg's fourteen files and the eight run three times in `stand-repeat` (test-plan §10) are the witness that the tree, ids and focus are unchanged, per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration.
- a11y ↔ layouts: both layout modes (incremental / non-incremental) must give the same tree and focus, per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Test harness pattern).

- The `a11y` leg (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y`, all fourteen files, `stand_accessibility_ids` and `stand_keyboard` among them) passes with no expectation edited (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).
- The inverted `dioxus_runtime_probe` pins assert, in both layout modes, that after the task's `set_focus` the engine focus, the snapshot's `focused` node and the tree's focus all name the target node (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation).
- Every Dioxus element node's `author_id` equals its stable element id after an initial build and after a re-render through the buffer, and `unkeyed_actionable` returns nothing on every stand task (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- `inert_subtree` passes, the focus fixup and the tree's fallback to the window holding (per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract).

body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: DioxusDocument's two render sites, initial_build (vdom.rebuild) and poll (vdom.render_immediate), run the vdom into a buffer of mutations while the document is not borrowed, then borrow the document once, replay the buffer through the existing MutationWriter, and flush the queued mounted events as before.
The point is that user code the vdom runs during render (a component body, a task it polls) can call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) with no RefCell already borrowed panic. This is an engine change for every Dioxus document: the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch and any app on the bridge.
Ports upstream's regression test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document into dioxus_document.rs's mod tests and makes it pass. It also inverts the probe's two should_panic hazard pins into tests that set_focus moves focus without a panic, in both layout modes, with their precondition still asserted first.
Re-verifies that behaviour is otherwise unchanged (the document built, element ids, snapshot and diff, the mounted events' order, incremental and non-incremental layout identity) through the existing stand_*, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle and the probe's other eight tests. Dioxus stays at 0.7, and none of upstream's 0.8-only parts are ported.

body_fields.what: the two render sites, initial_build and poll, and mod tests (the ported test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document)
the new buffer module that records 0.7's WriteMutations calls and replays them into MutationWriter

DioxusState, if the buffer lives on it as upstream's does; otherwise the file stays byte-identical to upstream at 434e0661
the two should_panic RefCell already borrowed pins (one per layout mode), inverted, and the file's module text
stale_node_mapping, re-run as a witness that the bridge's node mapping is unchanged
incremental_oracle, re-run as a witness of incremental and non-incremental layout identity

body: The Dioxus DOM bridge (packages/dioxus-native-dom): DioxusDocument, MutationWriter, DioxusState and the queued mounted events. The render path changes and must keep building the same document, element ids and mounted-event order.

DioxusDocument::element_id and element_ids (the four-tier stable ids), plus the accessibility snapshot, its text form and its diff. These must read the same after a buffered render, and the stand_* checks witness it.
A node the Dioxus bridge removes is dropped with its descendants and no longer resolves. Interaction state on removed nodes is cleared or retargeted. The replayed buffer must keep both.

Mutations go through DocumentMutator, which flushes deferred work on Drop and requests a redraw only for in-document mutations. Replaying the buffer under one borrow of the document must keep that flush and redraw behaviour.

Focus: MountedData set_focus reaches the engine's focus change (blur, focusout, focus, focusin) and the focus rules. The inverted pins and the ported test assert that focus moves to the named element.

The Dioxus version pin: Dioxus stays at "0.7.3" with dioxus-core 0.7.10 in the lock. No 0.8 move, no patched or vendored Dioxus crate and no pin bump. The buffer is written against dioxus-core 0.7's WriteMutations trait and VirtualDom::rebuild / render_immediate.

Two keyboard-types versions stand in the graph. A module that glob-imports dioxus::prelude::* names the workspace's crate as ::keyboard_types. Upstream's keyboard-types 0.8 move and keyboard_compat.rs removal are not ported.

The upstream-sync record: upstream 286874cc1 is read by git show in this checkout and ported in part. mutation_writer.rs stays byte-identical to upstream at 434e0661 where the port allows, and any change there is named with its reason.
Scenarios run in both layout modes, incremental and non-incremental, and must produce identical layouts. The inverted pins hold in both modes.

Nothing crosses: no verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, carrier, listener, port, env var, workspace crate, log field or span is added. The buffer holds ids, tag and attribute names and text in process only, and never prints or logs them.
Tracing in the engine and upstream crates is gated per call site with a cfg(not(feature = "tracing")) fallback. Any trace the buffer module keeps follows this rule and carries no mutation content.

Engine changes for every document are recorded as such, flagged upstreamable or not, with their merge surface. The buffered render is ratified as the founder's choice of fix and is an engine change for every Dioxus document.

Borrowing: the hazard is DioxusDocument::poll holding inner.borrow_mut() across vdom.render_immediate, while a polled task's set_focus borrows through doc_mut. Shared state is Rc<RefCell<…>>, and the fix takes the document's borrow only after the vdom returns.
The windowed dioxus-native launch and the browser and about pages built on Dioxus also render through DioxusDocument, so they take the buffered render. The windowed path is read, not run.

body_fields.convention: Unit tests sit in a #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the end of the source file, or in a #[path] child file of their own.

Each integration test file covers one behavior and opens with a //! doc naming it. Scenarios run in both layout modes. Tests first assert that the fixture produces the condition. blitz-tests keeps one test target per file.
Modules and files open with //! docs, public items carry ///, and doc comments state the rationale for constants. This applies to the new mutation_buffer.rs.

Formatting and lints: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings, and rustdoc warnings as errors, each run as a .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh leg. clippy::expect_used and clippy::unwrap_used each sit next to a justification.
Crate internals are pub(crate) or pub(super). The new buffer type stays crate-private unless the bridge's public API needs it.
unsafe blocks carry allow unsafe_code or a // SAFETY: comment. Borrow conflicts are worked around by taking a value out and restoring it.

body: The WPT runner, its outputs, bucketing and execution. The chunk changes only the Dioxus bridge, and WPT documents are not Dioxus documents.
The browser app's history store, SQLite persistence, favicon cache and URL suggester. None of these is touched by the render path.
JavaScript on Boa (blitz-vibey-script), its timers, module loader and bootstrap. A Dioxus document runs no page script.
blitz-net networking, its User-Agent, per-host semaphore and cache, and resource loading of stylesheets, images and fonts.
Painting and renderer backends: blitz-paint, the password mask, layer caps and the vello and skia selection.
The select model and the open select list: apply_select_choice, typeahead, reconcile_select_list and paint_select_list.
CSS approximations, unsupported features, inline SVG and the fonts decisions.
Deployment and packaging: publish-browser bundles, the Nix flake, Cross.toml and cross-compilation, signed builds and the WPT CI environments.
Release versioning, build profiles and the MSRV build-only job. No version, profile or rust-version moves.
The accesskit_xplat adapter and blitz-shell's windowing, IME and keyboard shortcuts.
HTML parsing through html5ever and xml5ever, and the HTML fixtures and fixture forms under examples/assets.
The project intent's UI graph capability. The UI graph is not built here.

relevant

- Dioxus stays "0.7.3" with no git dependency, no patch or vendored crate and no pin bumped; upstream `286874cc1` (Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3) waits for the next version and only its buffered render is ported onto the 0.7 bridge (per architecture §Project Intent and §Inherited Defaults).
- The MountedData hazard is recorded as a measured hazard with no engine change, its fix owned by this route entry: `DioxusDocument::poll` holding the document's `RefCell` across `render_immediate`. The chunk must turn that decision into an engine change for every Dioxus document, and the wrap must amend the decision (per architecture §Established Decisions → dec-dioxus-integration).
- Mutations reach the DOM only through the existing writer path, and `mutation_writer.rs` is held byte-identical to upstream at `434e0661`. A buffer replaying 0.7's `WriteMutations` calls has to feed that writer, not a second DOM write path. Whether the replay builds the same document as the direct write is research's question (per architecture §Standard Contracts → contract-dioxus-dom-bridge).
- The `mounted` listeners have to keep firing after `initial_build` and after each `poll`, in their present order, so the buffered apply must come before `flush_queued_mounted_events` (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → crosscut-event-processing).
- One incremental pipeline over versioned node ids: both layout modes must produce identical layouts, and the stable element ids and snapshot must not change (per architecture §Design Philosophy).
- The change adds no new workspace crate, env var, listener or public surface. The new buffer module stays inside `packages/dioxus-native-dom` as a crate-private (`pub(crate)`) module (per architecture §Occupied Resources and §Conventions).

- Shared state is `Rc<RefCell<…>>`, and borrow conflicts are avoided by taking data out and restoring it. Buffering the render and then taking the borrow once to apply it follows this (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns and §Conventions).
- DOM mutations go through `DocumentMutator`, which flushes deferred work on `Drop`. The buffered apply should keep using that one mutator path inside `MutationWriter` (per architecture §Conventions).
- Unit tests sit in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of the source file, which is where the ported `task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` belongs in `dioxus_document.rs`. An integration test file opens with a `//!` doc naming its behaviour and runs in both layout modes, so the module text of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_runtime_probe.rs` has to be re-said (per architecture §Conventions).
- New modules open with `//!` docs, and an ordering-sensitive block is marked "WARNING: DO NOT REORDER" (per architecture §Conventions).

- No 0.8-only parts of `286874cc1`: no stack-machine `WriteMutations`, no `StackWriter`/`BlitzBackend`, no keyboard-types 0.8 move, and no change to `Cargo.toml`'s Dioxus requirement (per architecture §Project Intent).
- The buffer's contents (ids, tag and attribute names, text) must not be logged or printed. No new log field or span, and no `NodeId` crosses the driver boundary (per architecture §Established Decisions → dec-driver-session).
- No `clippy::unwrap_used` or `clippy::expect_used` without a justification next to it in the new module (per architecture §Conventions).

- arch ↔ tests: the hazard pin in `dioxus_runtime_probe` is referenced from test-plan §6 E2E Test Strategy (per architecture §Established Decisions → dec-dioxus-integration). Inverting its two `should_panic` tests changes both plans.
- arch ↔ obs: the buffer must not reach telemetry. escher-telemetry's engine-target `SAFE_FIELDS` filter must not be widened (per architecture §Standard Contracts → contract-telemetry-bootstrap).
- arch ↔ all domains: the work stays in the locked crate `packages/dioxus-native-dom`, and no workspace crate is added (per architecture §Occupied Resources).

- `git diff 434e0661 HEAD -- packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` is empty, or each change is named with its reason (per architecture §Standard Contracts → contract-dioxus-dom-bridge).
- `Cargo.toml` still requires Dioxus "0.7.3", `Cargo.lock` still resolves dioxus-core 0.7.10, and no git dependency or vendored Dioxus crate is added (per architecture §Inherited Defaults).
- At wrap, the dec-dioxus-integration hazard fact is amended from "no engine change" to the buffered render, as an engine change for every Dioxus document (per architecture §Established Decisions).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` and rustdoc `-D warnings` stay green with the new buffer module (per architecture §Inherited Defaults).

body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: DioxusDocument's two render sites (initial_build's vdom.rebuild, poll's vdom.render_immediate) record the vdom's WriteMutations calls into a buffer with the document unborrowed, then take the document's borrow once, replay the buffer through the existing MutationWriter and flush the queued mounted events as before.
User code the vdom runs during render (a component body, a task it polls) can then call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) with no RefCell already borrowed panic; an engine change for every Dioxus document, the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch and any app on the bridge.
Ports upstream's regression test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document as the witness, and inverts dioxus_runtime_probe's two should_panic hazard pins into tests that the key-handler-spawned task's set_focus moves focus without panic in both layout modes, their precondition still asserted first.
Re-asserts behaviour otherwise unchanged (document built, element ids, snapshot and diff, mounted event order, incremental/non-incremental layout identity) through the existing stand_*, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle and the probe's other eight tests; Dioxus stays at 0.7, nothing crosses any boundary.

body: Focus as the engine holds it: the ported test and the inverted pins assert that set_focus(true) from a render-polled task moves focus to the named input, the key target first focused by Tab.
Element geometry read during render: get_client_rect on a held MountedData must answer from the document (box of the node) without panic; the ported test calls it.

Programmatic scroll reached through MountedData (scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size): the rule that a programmatic into-view scroll writes every nested scrolling box at once, behaviour applying to the viewport alone, must stay as it is once these calls are reachable during render.
The desktop-native surface: Dioxus apps open through dioxus_native::launch into a winit window; that windowed launch renders through the new buffer, its behaviour otherwise unchanged.
The web-spa surface: on wasm32 dioxus-native renders into a canvas on the page; as a Dioxus document it also renders through the buffer, unchanged in what it paints.

The browser app on desktop-native and mobile-native runs on the Dioxus bridge (any app on the bridge): its documents, element ids and mounted events must come out identical through the buffered render.
The two layout modes (incremental and non-incremental) the inverted pins run in, and their layout identity, which the change must keep.

The test harness's VirtualClock and settle as the probe's tests drive them: the inverted pins and the ported test run through the same harness and must not advance the clock or wait on animation beyond what the harness already does.

Text measurement in the blitz-tests crate: get_client_rect and focus assertions over text inputs depend on blitz-dom's system-fonts feature, without which text measures 0x0 and geometry assertions pass vacuously.
The buffer's content (ids, tag and attribute names, text) is in process only, never printed or logged, so no driver output, CLI line or log field changes.

a harness-driven test reads animation time only through the VirtualClock its documents read; settle never advances it, only advance moves it

The open select list's engine colour constants on SelectListView (highlight text and background, disabled text, border): no select list is touched.
Typography's type scale and engine text mapping, and the screenshot refusal fonts-unavailable: no font, text style or screenshot path changes.
Spacing values and the absent spacing scale: no spacing is set or read.
Border radius handling and its absent scale: untouched.
Depth strategy's elevation values and absent elevation scale: no shadows or stacking change.
Iconography: the browser toolbar SVG icons, IconButton, tab glyphs, icon size grid and favicons are not touched.
Cursor selection (CSS cursor keyword, Text, Pointer, Default): no pointer or cursor logic changes.
Mobile-native's component patterns (the urlbar, the back button, capture): the chunk changes no browser UI component.
Brand identity, anti-patterns, self-validation protocol and the design decisions log: no recorded intent, nothing for an engine render-path change to act on.

body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge in dioxus-native-dom: DioxusDocument's two render sites, initial_build (vdom.rebuild) and poll (vdom.render_immediate), run the vdom into an in-process buffer of 0.7 WriteMutations calls with the document unborrowed, then take the document's borrow once, replay the buffer through the existing MutationWriter and flush the queued mounted events as before.
A task polled during render can then call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to and the rest) with no RefCell already borrowed panic. The change reaches every DioxusDocument: the headless stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch and any app on the bridge.
Ports upstream's regression test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document as the witness, and inverts dioxus_runtime_probe's two should_panic hazard pins into tests that focus moves and nothing panics, in both layout modes.
Re-asserts that behaviour is otherwise unchanged, using the existing stand_*, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle and the probe's other eight tests as the witness. Dioxus stays at 0.7, and nothing crosses: no log field, span, env var or carrier.

body: dioxus-native-dom as an emitter: its log calls compile only behind the optional tracing feature, which dioxus-native's tracing feature turns on. Any log site the port adds or moves in the render path has to stay behind that feature, with a no-op path when it is off.

The mutation buffer holds ids, tag names, attribute names and values, and text node contents. These are page content, and they must never be printed, logged or put in a field. The buffer gets no Debug output that reaches a log line.

mutation_writer.rs's existing debug log sites record text node contents and attribute values as they are. The replay goes through the same MutationWriter, so those sites fire on the replay exactly as they did on the direct write. None is added, moved or widened, and the file stays byte-identical where the port allows.

The PII rule for engine targets: dioxus-native-dom's events reach escher's sink only when the engine tracing feature is on. There they are judged by the engine target allowlist, with only the safe fields printed. The port adds no new field name that the scrub would have to judge.
The flush of queued mounted events (flush_queued_mounted_events) keeps its order and its silence. The two callers change shape, but they add no log site, print or env read.

The ported witness test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document, inside dioxus-native-dom's own mod tests: it installs no subscriber, reads no env var and prints nothing. Its focus and client rect readings go into assertions only.

dioxus_runtime_probe in tests/blitz-tests: the two inverted tests and the other eight stay silent, with the silence census (print, env read, subscriber, escher_telemetry, listener) reading 0 over the file. A failure message names the layout mode and the outcome, never captured page text.

The invariant that nothing crosses: no verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, carrier, listener, port, env var, workspace crate, log field or span is added. The silence and census readings the plan records over the touched files and the stand checks stay as they are.

The sink checks host_log and mcp_log: the render path change reaches the escher-session host and its mcp role, so both still pass under both builds and read 0 id, name and typed-text needles at trace. escher-driver keeps its 2 info_span sites, and stand_act_spans keeps its eight fields.
The engine features by runner: a workspace build turns blitz-dom tracing on, while a -p blitz-tests or -p seven_guis build leaves it off. The new and inverted tests run silent under both.

The panic surface: the hazard that is removed was a RefCell already borrowed panic, and in seven_guis_native and escher-session a panic reaches the chaining escher-telemetry panic hook. The port adds no panic path, and no new failure path, in the render sites.

body: **2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — (the sink, the scrub, the panic hook) put escher-telemetry's allowlist scrub in place, where engine prefixes such as `dioxus_native` print only the seven safe fields. It also added the chaining native panic hook, after which std still prints the raw message, and set the rule that only the engine and upstream crates gate tracing behind the `tracing` feature. This chunk rests on all three. The RefCell panic it removes used to reach that hook. The mutation_writer trace sites that replay re-fires are judged by that scrub. The new buffer module must stay feature-gated, and escher-telemetry must stay unchanged.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — (the bridge's log-site citations) re-pointed the mutation_writer.rs citations in §6 Logged events and §8 Values logged as-is, and recorded the `trace!` count at 13 with no site added. This is the count and the citation set the buffered replay must leave unchanged with mutation_writer.rs kept byte-identical. It is also the precedent for re-pointing citations only, claims unchanged, if any line the plan cites moves.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — (Kept clause) recorded that dioxus-native-dom's unit tests appear in no obs-plan sentence, so their silence census was kept in the chunk's report only. This chunk puts the ported witness in dioxus_document.rs `mod tests`, and this is the precedent for where its 0 · 0 · 0 reading belongs.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — recorded that `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` derive `Debug`, which would print ids and typed text, and that nothing prints, logs or fields them. It set the rule: never field a type with `Debug`. That rule is the precedent for the chunk's anti-pattern: the buffer of ids, tags, attribute names and text must never be logged, fielded or `Debug`-dumped.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — (the second sink installer) made `escher-session` the second binary that installs the sink, beside `seven_guis_native`, and recorded a trap: a zero read from a host that installs no sink says nothing about one that does. The in-process witness and probe pins therefore cannot stand in for `host_log` / `mcp_log`. Those two read the sink-installing host that the buffered render now runs in.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — the sink drops every target outside the two prefix sets whole, `dioxus_core::*` and `dioxus_signals::*` included, and it set the rule that a target is admitted only together with a scrub rule for it. The cascade's binding relies on this: dioxus-core records stay dropped, and any site the port moves can reach the sink only as an engine-target event.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — (`command` span as built; `tracing` ungated in escher-driver) built the `command` span with its eight fields. It also recorded the two-build distinction: a workspace-wide build turns `blitz-dom/tracing` on, and a package-alone build leaves it off. That distinction is the basis for this chunk's "under both builds" acceptance and for the eight fields `stand_act_spans` re-asserts. The same chunk's PROVISIONAL entry added the closed-span record class and the rule that engine-target span pairs are judged by the safe-field rule.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — the founder ratified the closed span's line as the sink's second record class (2026-10-09). `host_log` and `mcp_log` count lines in this class, and the chunk re-asserts those counts unchanged.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — (the session host writes the command span; typed text measured in a host's log) made each hosted call write one closed `command` span. It measured the host by level under both builds, the workspace-built host writing one extra `blitz_dom::document` INFO line, with 0 id, name and typed-text needles. It also set the standing rule that a later surface adds no span or log field. These are the per-build readings the render change must leave as they are.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — added the `tool_call` span (`tool`, `ending`), with `command` nested as its child, and recorded the mcp role's stderr as 9 lines built alone and 10 workspace-built. The chunk keeps the 2 `info_span!` sites and these nesting and line counts.

body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: DioxusDocument's two render sites, initial_build (vdom.rebuild) and poll (vdom.render_immediate), run the vdom into an in-process buffer of 0.7 WriteMutations calls while the document is not borrowed, then take the document's borrow once, replay the buffer through the existing MutationWriter, and flush the queued mounted events as before.
The result is that user code the vdom runs during render (a component body, a task it polls) can call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) without a RefCell already borrowed panic. This is an engine change for every Dioxus document: the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch and any app on the bridge.
Ports upstream's regression test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document into dioxus_document.rs's tests, and turns the two should_panic hazard pins in dioxus_runtime_probe into tests that set_focus moves focus without a panic, in both layout modes, with their precondition still asserted first.
Dioxus stays at 0.7 (no crate added, patched, vendored or bumped). mutation_writer.rs stays byte-identical to upstream 434e0661 where the port allows. Nothing new crosses a boundary. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, and the existing stand_*, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle and other dioxus_runtime_probe tests are re-run as the witness.

body: The Dioxus 0.7 bridge's render path in dioxus-native-dom (DioxusDocument initial_build and poll): the document's mutable borrow is no longer held across vdom.rebuild or render_immediate. It is taken once to replay the buffer, and the mounted events are flushed in the same order as before.

The new mutation buffer (a new module in dioxus-native-dom): it holds element ids, tag and attribute names, attribute values and text in process only. It must never be printed, logged, put in a span or carried out by any carrier. This includes the values of password and file inputs, which the snapshot shows as MASKED_VALUE.

MountedData operations on the bridge (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size, in dioxus-native-dom's events.rs): they now run during render. The plan records how they degrade: try_doc returns None while the document is mutably borrowed, a missing node gives MountedError::OperationFailed, and NodeHandle node/node_mut panics on a node that does not exist. The new path must keep these rules and must not add a new panic path.

Dioxus mutations as an input-validation surface: data-dioxus-id is parsed as usize, unsupported attribute value types are ignored, falsy boolean attributes are removed, and dangerous_inner_html is applied with set_inner_html. Replaying the buffered calls into MutationWriter must keep all of these, in the original call order.

MutationWriter's id mapping (element_to_node_id unwraps; try_element_to_node_id returns an Option). The replay must not reach the unwrap with an id that is not yet mapped or is stale. The recorded panic paths for Dioxus nodes stay as listed, unless the port changes one, and then it is named with its reason.

The engine-change-for-every-Dioxus-document rule and the widening rule: the fix is ratified as the founder's choice and crosses no new boundary. No verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, carrier, listener, port, env var, workspace crate, log field or span is added.

Values the snapshot carries through the platform adapter, the driver's answers, MCP results and kept checks stay identical: the stable element id (the HTML id or a path, with no NodeId crossing), the masked password and file-input values, the snapshot text and its diff.

The dependency graph is unchanged: Dioxus stays at the 0.7.3 requirement (dioxus-core 0.7.10 in the lock), no 0.8 parts of upstream 286874cc1 are ported, and no package enters or moves in Cargo.lock. The cargo-deny audit leg and every cargo leg running with --locked must still pass over the changed code.

dioxus-native-dom's tracing feature (turned on by dioxus-native's tracing feature): any log site the port adds on the render path goes through the escher_telemetry allowlist sink and must not carry mutation content. The scope allows no new log field or span.

The hazard's mechanism as measured: poll holds inner.borrow_mut() across render_immediate, dioxus-core polls a queued task there, and set_focus borrows through doc_mut and panics. The inverted pins in dioxus_runtime_probe must show this is closed in both layout modes. The windowed dioxus-native path is read, not run.
The panic-guard tests the plan lists under graceful degradation (stale_node_mapping's guards against invalid SlotMap key and similar panics) are re-run unchanged as witnesses of the buffered render.

every cargo build and test the change runs, its new tests included, passes --locked and the cargo-deny audit leg, and no package enters Cargo.lock without being read name by name
an env var read by a new test is registered as test-only and non-secret under Environment values read
a panic, unwrap or expect path a change adds or removes in engine or bridge code is recorded under the Panic paths or Graceful degradation entries of error handling

CI workflow security (repository guards, the publish job's Signed Builds environment, signing material, WPT post-results trusted scripts, the token permissions on ci.yml): no workflow is edited.

rdme's markdown rendering with comrak unsafe raw HTML, and the WPT runner's local file reads and net provider: neither is on the Dioxus bridge.

body: **2026-10-31-engine-debts** — (the `MountedData` panic from a spawned task) first recorded in §Error Handling that a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal is first polled inside `render_immediate`, which holds the document's `RefCell`, so a `MountedData` call there panics `RefCell already borrowed`, any app able to meet it; Cells calls its handles synchronously to avoid it. This is the record the chunk closes, and the reason the fix is an engine change for every Dioxus document.

body:
Ports upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge in dioxus-native-dom: DioxusDocument's two render sites (initial_build's vdom.rebuild, poll's vdom.render_immediate) render into a buffer of 0.7 WriteMutations calls with the document unborrowed, then apply it once through the existing MutationWriter and flush the queued mounted events as before.
Adds a new buffer module (mutation_buffer.rs) and ports upstream's unit test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document into dioxus_document.rs's mod tests as the witness that a task polled during render can call MountedData (set_focus, get_client_rect) without a RefCell already borrowed panic.
Inverts the two should_panic hazard pins of dioxus_runtime_probe into tests that the key-handler-spawned task's set_focus moves focus and does not panic, in both layout modes, their precondition (handle held, key target focused by Tab) still asserted first.
An engine change for every Dioxus document; Dioxus stays at 0.7, no new log line, field or boundary crossing; behaviour otherwise unchanged, re-asserted by the existing stand_* checks, stale_node_mapping, incremental_oracle and dioxus_runtime_probe's other eight tests.

body: The dioxus-native-dom unit tests in the scope summary: the document's events, the mutation writer, the bridge, the stable element id and the snapshot, all of which build a DioxusDocument whose render path this chunk changes and must stay green.

The dioxus-native-dom crate-local test helper pattern: a DioxusDocument built with DocumentConfig::default(), initial_build, then mark_dirty and poll(None), the dioxus crate as dev-dependency; the ported unit test builds its document this way, and that config carries the no-op HTML parser.

The bridge_tests child module of dioxus_document (file dioxus_document_tests.rs), which reaches doc.vdom and doc.vdom_state directly; a buffer living on vdom_state or DioxusState changes what those tests construct over.
The Dioxus VirtualDom to DioxusDocument integration boundary, keyed_nodes_do_not_crash (100 inserts, main holding 100 children), a regression test over the same render path.
The element_id unit tests that a re-render-removed node no longer resolves and stands in no pair of element_ids(): the buffered replay must keep removal and mapping clearing identical.

The blitz-test-harness Dioxus constructors from_component and from_vdom and pump, which polls the document with no waker context: the inverted probe pins and every stand check reach the buffered poll through them.
The harness input helpers press (Tab and the handler's key) and the inspection helper focused, which the inverted pins use to assert their precondition and that focus moved.
The harness settle loop and its quiet-pass rule, which keeps poll's answer: the buffered poll must return the same answer so settle's Render, Loads and Layout readings do not move.
The differential oracle incremental_oracle and the both-layout-modes rule: the inverted pins run once per layout mode and the buffer must leave incremental and non-incremental layout identical.
The randomized stress stale_node_mapping (deterministic LCG, 1000 steps), the witness that buffered replay keeps slab and ElementId reuse correct.

The headless stand checks (stand_*) and the session over the stand, which boot DioxusDocument through seven_guis::stand: their snapshots, diffs, element ids and mounted-event order are the witness of unchanged behaviour.
The stand-repeat leg and its zero-failure flakiness budget: the stand checks and the seventeen named blitz-tests targets run three times with no retry over the new render path.
The coverage floor for packages/dioxus-native-dom at 83 percent line coverage, read by coverage_floor.py, with keyboard_compat.rs excluded: the new buffer module counts toward it.

The agent-run proof readings: run all's newest reading, 743 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored, with dioxus_runtime_probe picked up by run all with no script change; the inverted pins change their outcome, not the count, unless P4 measures otherwise.

The workspace test leg (cargo test --workspace --locked) and the windows and macos matrix test legs, which run the ported unit test and the inverted pins; the engine feature difference between the workspace and the per-package build (tracing, writing-mode) applies.
The local pre-push gate, ci-leg.sh fast (fmt, clippy, test, ci-scripts, embolden), which the change must pass.

The stand log format and the driver's one log line per call: the buffer holds ids, tag and attribute names and text in process only, so no new log line or field may appear and the line counts stay as measured.
The wall-time rule for checks: no sleep and no wall-clock read in a check unless its subject is wall time; the ported task test and the inverted pins drive time through the vdom and harness only.

body: **amd-3llbasfo** — 2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe: §6 records the MountedData hazard's mechanism re-measured at HEAD (`poll` holds `inner.borrow_mut()` across `vdom.render_immediate`, dioxus-core 0.7.10 polls the queued task there, `set_focus` borrows through `doc_mut` and panics). It adds the two `should_panic` pins `mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_panics_{non_incremental,incremental}`, with `hazard_ready` asserted first and the synchronous sibling `mounted_data_asked_at_once_in_a_key_handler_acts`, and routes the fix to «MountedData buffered render», with `task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` as its witness. This is the entry the chunk discharges: it must restate the mechanism as fixed and invert both pins, precondition still first.

The target has no `stand_` prefix and is none of stand-repeat's seventeen words or the a11y leg's fourteen. The entry also adds the §7 pages row (`toggled_listener`, `shared_state`, `hazard(spawned)`) and the §1 row of 10 tests, 8 looping both modes and 2 `should_panic`. The §1, §7 and §9 rows that state the `should_panic` pins must all be restated together.
